title: Recipe scaler with exact fractions (AI-only run task S2)

content.audience: Synthetic study task for the thesis AI-only run: a cook scaling a recipe
content.problem_statement: Scale a recipe's ingredient list by a whole number or fraction, keep every quantity exact, move to the larger unit when a quantity grows past it, and print the result. This is a frozen synthetic task for the thesis AI-only run, not a customer product.

user_flows.name: List as written
steps: Pipe an ingredient list into the CLI with no arguments
Read each ingredient with its quantity written in lowest terms and the count

user_flows.name: Scale
steps: Read the scaled quantities, moved to larger units where the rules say

user_flows.name: Bad line
steps: Pipe a list with a line the CLI cannot read
Read invalid line N and exit status 1

user_flows.name: Bad arguments
steps: Run with an argument the CLI does not accept
Read invalid arguments and exit status 2

scope: Python 3.8+ standard library only, entry point src/main.py, all code under src
Read all of stdin as text and split it into lines on \n, numbered from 1 counting every line. Split each line into whitespace-separated tokens; a line with no tokens is skipped

A WHOLE is 1 to 4 digits not starting with 0 (1 to 9999). A FRACTION is WHOLE/WHOLE, for example 3/4 or 5/2. A quantity is a WHOLE, a FRACTION, or a mixed number: a WHOLE token followed by a FRACTION token whose value is less than 1, for example 1 1/2

An ingredient line is a quantity, then UNIT, then NAME, and nothing else. UNIT is one of tsp, tbsp, cup, g, kg, ml, l, pc. NAME is lowercase ASCII words a-z joined by single hyphens, such as olive-oil
When a WHOLE is followed by a FRACTION token, the two always form a mixed number; if that fraction is 1 or more the line is invalid
--scale F multiplies every quantity, where F is a WHOLE or a FRACTION (not a mixed number). Without arguments the scale is 1. Arithmetic is exact (no floating point)

After scaling, convert to larger units in this order: tsp to tbsp (3 tsp = 1 tbsp), then tbsp to cup (16 tbsp = 1 cup), g to kg (1000 g = 1 kg), ml to l (1000 ml = 1 l). Each step applies when the quantity in the current unit is at least that many; so 48 tsp becomes 1 cup
Never convert to a smaller unit; pc is never converted

Print each ingredient in input order as QTY UNIT NAME. QTY is written in lowest terms: a whole number such as 2, a proper fraction such as 3/4, or a whole number, one space and a proper fraction such as 1 1/2
After the ingredients print N ingredients (or 1 ingredient when N is 1). With no ingredient lines print exactly: no ingredients. Each output line ends with \n. Exit 0
If any line is invalid print exactly: invalid line N, where N is the number of the first invalid line, print nothing else, and exit 1
Arguments are either none or exactly --scale F. Anything else prints exactly: invalid arguments, then \n, and exits 2
No files, network, environment variables or third-party packages

data_contracts.name: recipe/1
data_contracts.description: Synthetic ingredient lines on stdin; plain text list on stdout

acceptance_checks.statement: Without arguments print each ingredient in lowest terms and the count
--scale multiplies exactly and moves quantities to larger units by the stated rules

cases.stdin:
1 1/2 tsp salt
500 g butter
3 pc egg
cases.stdout:
1 tbsp salt
1 kg butter
6 pc egg
3 ingredients

acceptance_checks.statement: A line that cannot be read prints invalid line N for the first one and exits 1
Invalid arguments print invalid arguments and exit 2
